proposed.accounting: At logical tool operation start create one budget keyed by operation identity and captured S generation digest. Before a page reserve a shared potential-success page slot; before each kubeRequest invocation reserve an attempt. Reservation/commit must be synchronous and atomic in the existing event loop, no async await inside it. Oversized retries retain the page reservation and consume another attempt; successful parsed API page commits exactly one page (including empty page). Terminal failure releases uncommitted page reservation but does not refund attempts. Thus concurrent branches cannot each spend the full shared cap. No global service/run quota is inferred from a peroperation budget. When all remaining page capacity is only temporarily reserved by in-flight branches (successfulPages<maximumPages), later branches wait in FIFO order for reservation release/commit under the SAME absolute deadline; they must not report page-limit exhaustion solely because slots are temporarily occupied. When successfulPages reaches cap or attempts/deadline is exhausted, close admission and resolve queued branches as partial/not-started. Release/commit each reservation exactly once; late aborted responses cannot commit pages.
proposed.deadlines: Capture one monotonic absolute aggregate deadline once. Finite local calls also capture their deadline once; oversized retry retains it. Effective request timeout/abort is the minimum of existing perGET timeout, remaining finite-call deadline and remaining shared deadline. Remaining<=0 means no GET. Budget expiry cancels in-flight GETs using the same original selected API/CA/token transport, not a replacement server or timeout reset. Current code uses Date.now; monotonic shared cancellation is proposed implementation. Recheck the same budget after per-request token/CA file reads and immediately before actual HTTPS dispatch, so a delayed file read cannot start a GET after deadline. Expiry is an admission/cancellation boundary, not a claim of hard realtime timer scheduling: measure requested deadline, actual dispatch/abort callbacks and native scheduling separately. Do not enlarge configured deadline to absorb test lateness. Already observed native API/auth/JSON failures keep their rejecting priority.
proposed.stopAndOutput: On shared page/attempt/deadline limit, stop starting GETs and preserve each original continuation. Return partial with explicit scan_page_limit/scan_attempt_limit/scan_deadline and perresource started/pages/continuation/completeness (complete|partial|not-started). Unstarted empty results never prove absence. Nonbudget API/auth/JSON/oversized-single-item errors retain actual rejecting boundary; do not convert403/401/network errors into successful partial data. Existing mapItem and selectors/continue token remain internal task/result processing. A finite local one-page call deadline has its own partial reason finite_call_deadline and original cursor/completeness; it must cancel the active real request instead of merely checking time after a late successful response. The aggregate budget may be unbounded in this diagnostic: local expiry does not invent a shared cap. Preserve API/auth/JSON native errors as rejecting boundaries.
proposed.retryInvariant: Only KUBERNETES_RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE causes integer-halving down to1 with unchanged selectors/continuation and unchanged maxBytes. Transport errors do not retry. Fail if one item still exceeds ceiling. Failed attempts do not increment successful pages.
proposed.boundsJustification: Current pageSize guard has no safe upper bound; proposed explicit policy supports exactly representable positive safe integers and rejects coercion/unsafe JSON integers before effects. No arbitrary500 const or parser clipping. Page/attempt caps are exact positive safe counters. Single-page maxPages1 remains operation pagination ABI, not an invented default writer.
proposed.isolatedFiniteCallControl: P4-L3 complete A30/B15 variants keep aggregate modeunbounded and perGET timeout10000ms. Each original HTTPS response phase takes7000ms; oversized page4→2→1 produces A successful third request at~21s before30s, but B cancels third near15s. No aggregate5s or perGET10s boundary preempts the finite local budget. This is real client/TLS library definition evidence, not native Kubernetes/RBAC proof.
